title.narrative: Life saving Response to unaddressed the Nutrution and dispalcement needs in Amhara Region Raya Kobo Woreda

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian situation in Ethiopia has been characterized as complex and protracted putting millions of people in need of humanitarian assistance. In particular, the northern part of the country (Tigray and Amhara) is severely affected by overlapping and multiple crises, whereby the drought condition coupled with the impact of the prolonged conflict increases food insecurity and malnutrition. These conditions have devastated farms, and depleted rivers and water sources, pushing communities and their livestock into an exacerbated humanitarian crisis marked by severe shortages of food, water, and fodder. This has led to heightened levels of malnutrition and increased health and protection risks. Access to health services, medical supplies, and trained health workers remains limited in Ethiopia and creates gaps in responding to disease outbreaks, resulting in widespread hunger and malnutrition among severely affected communities. There is ongoing concern regarding the high level of malnutrition in particular at Raya Kobo Woreda. The proposed woredas are experiencing extreme levels of malnutrition. ltbrgtThe average Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rates for under-five children, SAM, MAM and pregnant/lactating women are reported at 39%, 28% and 37% in the targeted woreda (PIE MIRA Assessment Report, July 2024). Insufficient food for mothers and caretakers at health centers, lack of safe drinking water supply, poor sanitation coverage, and limited hygiene facilities contribute to these concerns. Late weather, rainfall and early drought have resulted in poor crop and pasture performance in the targeted woredas. The most pressing health and nutrition needs reported are the treatment of malnutrition, malaria, poor quality health services, diarrhea, and mental health services. Immediate and coordinated efforts are needed to alleviate the severe impact of malnutrition in these areas and improve overall health outcomes. These underscore the need for targeted intervention and comprehensive strategy to provide integrated humanitarian assistance and reduce malnutrition aiming to improve nutritional practices and overall health outcomes. Plan International Ethiopia will focus on ensuring equitable access to quality preventive and curative nutrition services within the integrated sectoral framework where the other sectoral interventions contribute directly and indirectly to malnutrition furthermore the project aims to provide comprehensive/holistic services to address the multitude of needs of the affected community.ltbrgtPlan International Ethiopia designed this intersectoral response to the increasing humanitarian needs of drought-affected host communities including IDPs in Raya kobo woreda. The project aims to reduce malnutrition through life-saving nutrition, health, WASH, and agricultural assistance along with enhancing the mainstreaming of protection and gender in humanitarian action. The project aims the provide integrated services encompassing health, nutrition, WASH and agriculture components to reduce malnutrition but also meet their basic needs, improve their health conditions, enhance household livelihood to improve food security and increase their overall well-being. The health section will focus on immunization, disease outbreaks and control measures through logistic and operational support to mobile health teams in targeted outreach sites, reinforcing existing health facilities by building their capacity. In lighting the burden of malnutrition in affected communities, addressing the critical WASH needs at the facility and community level which is affected by the drought but also overlay with the protracted impact of the prolonged conflict that the project aims to address during the project period. Such action is intended to address the community WASH needs aiming to contribute to malnutrition reductionltbrgtlt/pgt
